dedupe_keys.name: fcc csric best practices for communications security and reliability

description: The Communications Security, Reliability and Interoperability Council advises the Federal Communications Commission on the security and reliability of communications systems, including telecommunications, media and public safety, and this dataset is its searchable collection of 1,129 best practices. Each best practice has a number, a description, a reference, keywords, a priority level, the network types it applies to (wireless, wireline, cable, satellite, internet and data, public safety) and the industry roles concerned (service provider, network operator, equipment supplier, property manager, government), covering topics such as backup power, physical and cyber security, network diversity, disaster preparedness and recovery, 911 and emergency alerting. Coverage: guidance applicable to US communications networks, compiled over successive councils and last updated in December 2022. Format and access: a table through the Socrata API with CSV export and a search tool, free as US government data. Caveats: best practices are voluntary and not measured; text is condensed and cross-references older councils' reports. Simulation uses: governance inputs and assumptions on backup power, diversity and restoration practices for resilience and emergency response models of telecom networks. Related records: FCC DIRS status reports show outcomes in disasters, and the ENISA incident reports give European incident causes.
